newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X Minerals sinks on Busang report.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X Minerals sinks on Busang report.

text.p: Shares in Canadian prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd fell sharply on Friday after an Indonesian newspaper report cast doubt on the size of the rich Busang gold deposit.

Bre-X's stock, which was halted earlier today, fell 2.80 to a 52-week low of 14.65 after it resumed trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Bre-X was the TSE's most active stock with turnover of 3.6 million shares.
On Nasdaq, Bre-X shares were off 1-3/4 at 10-7/8 after earlier hitting a low of 10-1/4.

Shares in Bre-X were halted after a report in Indonesia's Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper, citing unnamed sources, that a review by Busang partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc showed the deposit was smaller than Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces of gold.
However, a Freeport official said on Friday that the company's due diligence is not finished.
"We have made no public report. We are not making any report until the due diligence is completed," Freeport vice-president of communications Garland Robinette said in a telephone interview.
The newspaper said a source at PT Askatindo Karya Minerals, one of the Indonesian partners in Busang, also said Freeport's findings did not match Bre-X's estimates.
Bre-X issued a statement on Friday that PT Askatindo officials confirmed to the Canadian company that they have not completed their due diligence or commented to the press.
New Orleans-based Freeport-McMoRan holds 15 percent of Busang and the right to mine the deposit. Calgary-based Bre-Minerals, which discovered the deposit, has 45 percent.
The rest of Busang is owned by the Indonesian government and two Indonesian companies.
Toronto-based Minorca Resources, which has a royalty interest in the deposit, was also halted on the TSE. Minorca was off 1.35 at 4.00 on 356,000 shares after it resumed trading.
Analysts said the Indonesian press report, coming a few days after the tragic death of Bre-X's chief Busang geologist, may have prompted investors to bail out of the stock.
Michael de Guzman, who fell out of a helicopter on Wednesday on his way to the Busang gold property, was ill and may have committed suicide, Indonesian officials have said.
Search crews have not yet found de Guzman's body.

"Obviously, one of the reasons the stock has been under a lot of pressure is because of this mystery of the man's death. He was their chief on-site exploration guy...which cast some doubt on the stock," said PaineWebber analyst Marc Cohen.

"Let's have the due diligence completed and then we'll know in reality what this is. But given the amount of money made by people who owned it from the beginning, you can understand they want out of the stock," Cohen said.
